name: Risograph Print
summary: A three-ink risograph zine: fluorescent pink, blue and yellow overprinting on recycled paper, out of register, with halftones and drum grain.
description: Everything is printed with only three fluorescent soy inks – pink #ff48b0, medium blue #0078bf and yellow #ffe800 – on off-white recycled paper. There is no black plate and no outline anywhere: shapes are flat ink layers that multiply where they overlap (pink over blue turns violet, pink over yellow red-orange, blue over yellow green), and every plate sits a few pixels out of register, so edges show slivers of single inks and paper. Tones come from coarse round halftone dots on a different screen angle per ink or from random grain stipple, and a drum texture of clumps, streaks, missing-ink specks and soft banding runs through every layer. The UI is a zine page: crop marks, registration targets, colour bars, stamped labels and offset ink blocks.
bestFor: colourful top-down action and arcade games
indie games with a zine or poster identity
menus, title cards and promo art
avoidFor: night scenes that need deep blacks
UI-dense simulations that need many neutral greys

difficulty.why: A new asset is a short list of flat shapes, each assigned to one or two of three inks, plus one halftone gradient – overprint colours, misregistration, grain and paper come from the shared plate engine. The craft is choosing which shapes knock out and which overprint, and keeping silhouettes readable without any outline.

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D (procedural, no image assets): three ink plates per sprite in one RGB mask canvas -> per-pixel multiplicative bake with drum grain -> cached sprites; ground shaded per pixel in cached chunks
technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = clamp(round(screenHeight x dpr / 360 x 1.6), 3, 8) px per world unit; the ground at up to 2.5 px per world unit, scaled with nearest-neighbour so halftone dots stay crisp.
technique.summary: Each sprite is drawn into one mask canvas whose red, green and blue channels are the pink, blue and yellow plates ('lighter' adds ink, multiplying by #00ffff / #ff00ff / #ffff00 knocks one plate out), every plate translated by its own misregistration offset. A bake computes paper x product over inks of (1 - coverage x density x grain x (1 - ink)) per pixel.
technique.linework: None. No outlines and no black. The only lines are shapes in their own right: mouths, stems, grass ticks and hand scribbles 0.5-0.8 units wide in a single ink, also misregistered.
technique.shading: Flat ink plus halftone: round AM dots (pitch 1.3 units on sprites, 2.6 on the ground; radius = pitch x 0.707 x sqrt(tone)) at screen angles 15° pink, 75° blue, 45° yellow, or FM grain stipple (0.5-unit cells). Volume is a second ink overprinted as a halftone gradient – blue dots on pink become violet shading, yellow dots on blue a green lit side.
technique.lighting: No light, only print: a 'lit' side is a lighter halftone or a yellow overprint, a shadow is a blue halftone ellipse multiplied onto the ground. Yellow halftone discs stand in for glow.
technique.texture: Recycled paper (#f3ede0 with 2 % grain and rare fibre flecks) plus a 256 x 256 drum-grain tile per ink: clumps, vertical streaks, ±7 % noise, 2.8 % missing-ink specks; ink density mottling (±12 %) and horizontal banding (±5 %).

palette.role: What a solid blue layer prints as

paletteRules: Only three inks exist. Every other colour must be a product of them on paper – never mix a new hex value by hand.
Overprints multiply: pink x blue = violet #312d7f, pink x yellow = red-orange #f3480d, blue x yellow = green #317d0e, all three = near black #312a0a.
There is no black ink and no grey; the darkest value is the violet overprint (or the three-ink near black in tiny spots).
White is paper: highlights, eyes and teeth are knockouts where no plate prints.
The ground uses light tints (tones 0.1-0.5) so characters in solid ink always sit on top; solid ground ink only for ponds and small decals.
Each plate keeps its own misregistration offset everywhere: pink (+0.72, -0.46), blue (-0.60, +0.48), yellow (+0.30, +0.66) world units.

typography.role: Titles, the big title panel, counters, bar labels, floating numbers
typography.css: font: 400 34px/1 'Rubik Mono One', monospace; color: #0078bf; text-shadow: 3px 2px 0 rgba(255,72,176,.88);

typography.role: Card titles and general sans text
Small print: captions, labels, card body copy, hints – letter-spaced uppercase
typography.css: font: 500 11px/1.2 'DM Mono', monospace; letter-spacing: .34em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #0078bf;

world.summary: A risograph print of a park seen from above: off-white paper with soft pink and yellow halftone tint clouds that fade out in growing dots, hand-cut colour fields of meadow (green-dotted rosette) and blossom (pink dots), winding yellow halftone paths and solid blue ponds with paper wave marks and a blue halftone shore. Every region edge shows three slightly different outlines because each plate is offset. Decals and props gather in clumps and groves, with calm paper between them.
layers: Paper #f3ede0 with 2 % grain and rare fibre flecks

Tint clouds on bare paper: AM halftone fades on the pink (up to tone 0.30) and yellow (up to 0.26) screens – the dots grow toward the cloud core (tone = ((cloud − 0.3) × 1.43)² × max), the printed riso gradient
Meadow fields: yellow halftone 0.27 + blue halftone 0.11 (different screen angles) + a faint blue stipple (≤ 3.5 %)
Blossom fields: pink halftone 0.25 + a light yellow stipple (≤ 12 %)
Paths ~40 units wide: yellow halftone 0.46 with a 2 % pink speckle; they knock out the fields below
Ponds: solid blue with dashed wavy paper lines (7.5-unit spacing), a blue halftone shore fading over 9 units outside

Decals as extra ink on the plates, kept only in clumps (noise /120, smoothstep 0.48–0.7) and as blue grass drifts along every region edge: blue grass ticks, five-dot flowers with overprinted centres, pink pebbles on paths, yellow lily pads on ponds (they print green)
Every plate shifted by its misregistration; drum grain, density mottling and banding over all of it

characters.summary: Bold, simple shapes built from flat ink layers with no outline, printed on their own paper (knocked out of the world) so they read on any ground. The main character (~19 x 34 units with the bobble) is a kid in a yellow beanie with a red-orange cuff and pink bobble, a blue hoodie shaded with pink halftone (violet dots), violet trousers and red-orange sneakers, a peach halftone face with violet eyes and a pink cheek; when dashing they first crouch (anticipation), then ride a red-orange skateboard with blue wheels. The main character has 8 computed walk poses with two-bone knees, 3 breathing poses, a crouch, a skateboard pose and a recoil. Small creatures are gumdrop blobs (pink with a yellow bobble antenna, or blue with pink horns) with paper eyes, stubby arms and stepping feet, 6 waddle poses; fast creatures are scribbled ghosts – a pale tint silhouette filled with blue and pink hand scribbles; the large creature is a geometric monster: a blue triangle with an overprinted pink disc belly, one big yellow eye, a near-black mouth with paper teeth and a pink horn.
rules: No outlines: the silhouette is the edge of the inks. Keep a dark overprint (violet) somewhere on every character for contrast.
Back limbs are printed one ink darker (violet or three-ink) than front limbs – depth without lines.
Eyes, teeth and highlights are paper knockouts; pupils are violet (pink + blue).
Shade with a second ink as a halftone gradient (blue dots on pink, yellow dots on blue, pink dots on blue) – never with a darker version of the same ink.
Characters are knocked out of the world: baked onto their own paper and drawn opaque, so a blue creature on a blue pond stays readable.
Sizes: main character ~19 x 34, small creature 18 x 18, fast creature ~20 x 20 floating 4 units up, large creature ~54 x 60.

Main character pose table: feet (with lift), arm angles, body bob, head lag, pompom lag and lean. The upper body is printed in a space that bobs and leans around the hip point (Press.at), the head adds its own lag; knees are solved from hip-ankle distance (leg length 7.9).
Secondary parts lag the body: the pompom swings after the head, the bobble antenna and the horns after the critter's squash (phase delay 1.5–1.8 rad).

props.summary: Scenery made of a few flat shapes that overprint the ground with multiply: round trees (a yellow disc and a smaller blue disc overlapping into a green lens, pink fruit dots), a pink lollipop tree with yellow grain, pines of stacked blue triangles with a yellow halftone lit side, bushes of overlapping yellow and blue circles, halftone-blue rocks and small violet pebbles, little houses (pink walls and a blue roof, or yellow walls and a pink roof, with knocked-out window crosses), flower clusters, a potted leafy plant and a street lamp with a yellow halftone glow disc.
rules: Overlap shapes of different inks on purpose: the overlap is the most riso part of any prop.
Props print with multiply over the ground, so a pink house on a yellow path gets a red-orange base – keep their own inks solid so they still read.
Use 2-3 inks per prop, one halftone gradient at most.
Each prop has a blue halftone shadow ellipse shifted slightly right.
Trees, flowers and plants sway by shearing (±0.02); houses and rocks are static.
Typical sizes: tree 24 x 42, pine 26 x 44, house 28 x 30, bush 20 x 16, lamp 3 x 37 with a 21-unit glow.

effects.name: Ink pellet projectile
effects.how: A pink disc (r 2.7) with an overprinted yellow core (prints red-orange) and a trail of three shrinking pink halftone dots, rotated along the flight direction and multiplied onto the world.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small: a yellow diamond (6.8 x 9.6) with a smaller overprinted pink diamond – red-orange core, yellow and pink fringes. Large: a pink five-point star with a blue overprint centre and a yellow halftone gradient, gently tilting; both bob 3 units above a tiny halftone shadow.

effects.name: Orbiting sun stamp
effects.how: A yellow disc with blue dot eyes and a smile, pink halftone shading, inside a separately rotating ring of 10 pink zigzag rays; a yellow halftone glow ellipse prints on the ground below.

effects.name: Registration-target impact
effects.how: On a hit a registration target (circle + crosshair, 0.75-unit lines) appears in pink and blue, each at its plate offset, growing from 2.5 to 7.5 units while the two plates drift further apart and fade within 0.22 s; plus three ink dots.

effects.name: Ink burst
effects.how: A 12-point starburst in one ink with a radial halftone of a second ink and a paper hole in the middle, popping with an overshoot; a mono-ink splat blob with satellite droplets prints on the ground and fades over 0.8 s; a ring of halftone dots in two misregistered inks grows to ~25 units; 6-14 triangle confetti in the three inks tumble and fall.

effects.name: Plate separation
effects.how: Appearing creatures arrive as their three single-ink plates sliding into register one after another (yellow, pink, blue) over 0.45 s while a misregistered registration target marks the ground; vanishing creatures pop yellow, then their plates drift apart along three directions up to 13 units and fade.

effects.name: Misregistration jolt
effects.how: When hit, a character is overlaid with a yellow 'pop' copy, shoved 2.6 units along the blow and tilted 0.22 rad away, and its pink and blue plates kick 3-4 units out of register, then settle back as the flash decays (~0.15 s).

effects.name: Glow-up rings
effects.how: Large flat rings of 26 yellow and pink halftone dots expand over the ground, a second blue-pink ring at body height, and eight yellow four-point sparkles with a pink misregistered copy fly out.

atmosphere.summary: No light and no fog – the atmosphere is the print itself: the screen is a zine page with a recycled-paper margin (2.4 % of the screen height) carrying crop marks, three registration targets and a colour bar of solids, overprints and tints, all printed in the three inks out of register. A faint paper veil adds drum banding across the image and ink starvation towards the right edge.
rules: Shadows are blue halftone ellipses multiplied onto the ground (alpha 0.7-0.85), never dark blurs.
Glow is a yellow halftone disc or ellipse, never an additive light.
Keep the page margin, crop marks and registration targets – they frame every view.
The banding veil stays under 6 % paper opacity; it should be felt, not seen.
No vignette, no blur, no colour grading beyond the inks.

ui.summary: UI is a zine layout: panels are paper blocks with an offset ink block behind them (blue, pink or yellow, 5-9 px) as if a plate slipped, crop marks at every corner, registration targets beside titles and counters, stamped round labels, yellow title strips with blue mono type and a pink misregistered shadow, halftone bars whose fill multiplies over the dots, and cards with a halftone colour band (multiply-blended dots) and the icon on a paper stamp disc.

motion: Main character walk: 8 computed poses per stride at anim x 0.4 x 8 – contact, down, passing, up for each leg; the swing foot lifts 2.4 units and its knee bends, body bob 0.9·sin(2ph), arms counter-swing ±0.95 rad, lean 0.06; the head (0.9 rad delay) and the pompom (1.8 rad) follow through. An ink fleck kicks up on every contact pose.
Idle: 3 held breathing poses picked on an eased 2.6 s clock (lingers at both ends); shoot squash 4.5 %.

Dash: one crouch pose while dashT > 0.165 (anticipation), then the skateboard pose leaning 0.24 rad forward, two fading single-plate copies (blue, pink) 7 and 14 units behind and four pink speed streaks. Hurt: a recoil pose (thrown back, arms up) plus the misregistration jolt.

Small creature: 6 waddle poses at anim x 0.85 (+ seed phase) – feet lift 1.5, squash at contact / stretch on passing baked in, arms counter-swing, antenna and horns lag; runtime |sin| hop of 1.4 units and ±0.07 rad rock. Large creature: 4-frame stomp at anim x 0.32 with 6 % contact squash.

Fast creature: 6 tail frames at 8 fps (offset by seed), hovering 2.6–6.0 units on an eased triangle curve with a 2.4 s period per ghost – it lingers at the top and bottom instead of a sine bob; the scribbles re-draw per frame so the fill boils like hand animation.
Appearing: plates slide into register yellow -> pink -> blue over 0.45 s from up to 14 units away; vanishing: plates drift apart up to 13 units in 0.35 s.

Hit: 0.15 s yellow pop, a 2.6-unit knock-back shove and 0.22 rad tilt away from the blow (easing with flash²), pink and blue plates kicked 3 units out of register. Invulnerable blink: the pink and blue plates slip 2.4 units out of register every other 1/12 s – never transparency.
UI: titles 'pull' in from a 22 px offset with a widely misregistered pink shadow that settles in 0.5 s; cards slide in staggered by 70 ms.
do: Build every asset from flat shapes, each assigned to one, two or three of the three inks.
Let overlaps multiply on purpose – the overprint colours are the palette.
Offset each plate by its own few-pixel misregistration, consistently across the whole game.
Shade with halftone dots of a second ink at that ink's screen angle, or with grain stipple for soft gradients.
Knock out eyes, teeth and highlights to bare paper.
Run drum grain, missing-ink specks and slight banding through every layer, including the UI icons.
Frame the screen as a printed page: paper margin, crop marks, registration targets, colour bar.
Drive the main character from a pose table: 8 computed walk poses with bent knees, a breathing idle, a crouch before the dash and a recoil; let the pompom and antennas lag.
dont: Don't draw outlines or use black – this is not a comic and not a carved print.
Don't invent extra colours; if a colour cannot be made from pink, blue and yellow on paper it does not belong.
Don't use smooth airbrush gradients, glows or blur – tones are dots or grain.
Don't register the plates perfectly; a crisp perfect print looks like flat vector art.
Don't fill the ground with solid ink – keep it light so solid-ink characters stay on top.
Don't use fine, tiny halftone screens; the dots must be visible at a glance (≥ 1.3 units).
Don't add 3D lighting, specular highlights or drop shadows with blur.
Don't spread FM speckle or decals evenly over the whole page – fade tints with halftone dots and gather details in clumps.
performance: Baked once at init: 5 main-character poses, 2 x 4 small-creature frames, 4 scribbled ghost frames and 4 large-creature frames (each with a paper print, a yellow pop copy and three single-ink plates), 10 props (print + multiply layer), collectibles, projectile, sun stamp, 9 splats, 3 bursts, shadow and glow – roughly 150 ms at K = 4. Per frame: one drawImage per actor (plus 3 plates only while appearing, vanishing or flashing), multiply drawImages for props, shadows and effects, cheap arcs for dots, rings and confetti, and 5 drawImages for the page frame and banding veil. Ground chunks (256 units) are shaded per pixel in a generator spread over frames: ~70 ms per chunk at 2.5 px/unit, with a per-cell fast path when a whole cell lies inside one region.
